thread:
alex: Heads up — my sampleapp started failing the rerank flow after I wired in the new batching helper. Getting a vector dim mismatch from the rerank endpoint. Repro steps below, anyone seen an off-by-one in embedding dims?

alex: repro (node):
```js
// using embedBatchHelper from sdk 0.8.2
const batches = embedBatchHelper(inputs, {batchSize: 8});
const res = await client.embeddings.create({model: 'embed-small', input: batches[0]});
console.log(res.data[0].embedding.length); // => 1535 but should be 1536
```

devon: @alex can you paste the exact error you get from the rerank call? is the embedding array truncated or is the server complaining? :eyes:

alex: rerank call error (truncated):
```
Error: RerankRequestInvalid: embedding vector length mismatch (expected 1536, got 1535)
    at validateRerankPayload (/srv/app/node_modules/redwood-rerank/index.js:92:15)
```
The embeddings response from the embeddings endpoint is already 1535 long — so the rerank endpoint rejects it. I suspect the batching helper is producing a Float32Array length calc bug when a single-item batch is used.

kaya: iirc there was a bug in the JS helper where we computed byteLength / 4 but accidentally used bytes for the element count in one codepath. That would cause a -1 for certain lengths when padding logic kicks in. Which sdk version are you on?

alex: 0.8.2. I can try 0.8.3 if that's fixed.

kaya: confirmed — fix landed in 0.8.3. TL;DR: batch helper used `buffer.length` instead of `buffer.byteLength` in the last-chunk padding routine, so TypedArray slicing could drop the final float. Workaround: after calling the helper, add an assertion: `if (embedding.length !== modelDim) throw new Error(...)` or pad with a zero float. Example patch:
```js
// quick local workaround
const out = await client.embeddings.create(...);
if (out.data[0].embedding.length !== 1536) {
  out.data[0].embedding = [...out.data[0].embedding].concat(new Array(1536 - out.data[0].embedding.length).fill(0));
}
```

devon: can you also paste the raw wire payload you sent to rerank? need to check the expected schema. The rerank endpoint expects `{"candidates": [[... vectors ...]], "queries": [[...]]}` (array of arrays). If embed helper returns flattened buffers in some edge case we might be serializing wrong.

alex: raw body I sent (trimmed):
```json
{"queries":[[0.001, -0.002, ..., 0.123]], "candidates":[[[...]]]}
```
So it looks correctly nested, just vector length off by one.

josh: adding to this — we also saw a sporadic response format difference between runtimes: some languages return `embedding` as an Array of floats, others return a base64 encoded Float32 buffer in `embedding_bytes`. If client code assumes one form it can truncate or mis-parse. Which client did you use for deserialization?

alex: node SDK did the deserializing. I logged the shape after SDK returns it (embedding is JS Array of numbers). No base64 here.

kaya: action items:
- devex will cut a patch to the batch helper to use `byteLength` consistently and add an assertion in the helper tests.
- josh / eng-ml will add server-side validation that returns a more explicit error payload: `{"expected_dim":1536, "got":1535, "field":"queries[0]"}` so it's easier to map.
- devex-bot created INF-4567 for the SDK fix: <https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4567|INF-4567> :white_check_mark:

devex-bot: Created ticket INF-4567: "js embed batch-helper off-by-one causing rerank dim mismatch" assigned to @kaya.

alex: tried local patch from `npm i @redwood/sdk@0.8.3-rc1` and it fixed the length — rerank accepted payload. Thanks all. :relieved:

kaya: i'll roll the patch to stable 0.8.3 today and add a small migration note in the SDK changelog about the padding behavior.

devon: leaving this thread here for folks hitting similar symptoms — short checklist: upgrade SDK, validate embedding length before rerank, and file ticket if you see `embedding_bytes` vs `embedding` format mismatch.

alex: closing for now. will reopen if anything else crops up. :thumbsup:
